Subject: Operational evidence request: no-adaptive-modeling assurance & transfer paths

Hi Sarah / Marco —

Thanks again for the productive call yesterday. For the DPA redlines and procurement checklist we need concrete operational artifacts to accept the no-adaptive-modeling / no-training commitment and to sign off on cross-border transfer controls. Can you confirm whether you can provide the following by EOW?

Required items (we will attach to the DPA appendix):
- Current subprocessor inventory (CSV) with hosting geography and purpose
- SOC 2 (or equivalent) snapshot or access to the portal (PDF acceptable)
- Short ops note describing onshore routing for EU-covered accounts (SFTP/region-aware routing or equivalent)
- Confirmation on KMS approach: customer-managed keys (BYOK) vs. provider KMS + residency
- Sample audit log extract showing that model improvement pipelines are segregated / disabled for our tenant (redacted is fine)

Optional but helpful:
- A brief runbook for your no-learning workflow (how requests are flagged, KV cache handling, and retention)
- Any DocuSign/checkbox language you prefer for a no-training addendum

I’ve attached a marked-up DPA with the redlines we discussed (redlines_20280604.pdf). If you can share the subprocessor CSV and SOC2 snapshot, we can route to our legal and security teams for final sign-off. If any item needs extra time, flag which ones — we can scope a contingent evidence path instead of blocking the whole agreement.

Thanks —
Karthik
Director, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redlines_20280604.pdf (PDF, 92 KB)
From: Sarah Johnson <sarah.johnson@northleaf.com>

Subject: Re: Operational evidence request: no-adaptive-modeling assurance & transfer paths

Hi Karthik —

Appreciate the clear checklist. We can provide most of this; a few clarifying Qs to make sure we deliver the right artifacts:

1) Subprocessor CSV: we have a canonical list (includes a staged analytics vendor and a managed SFTP partner). Do you need historical access dates or just the current roster?
2) SOC 2: we can deliver the Q1 snapshot as a PDF (we'll attach). Full portal access requires an NDA — is the PDF sufficient?
3) Audit log extract: we can provide a 7-day redacted extract that shows pipeline toggles and user/service account interactions. Is redaction by tenant id OK?
4) KMS approach: for EU accounts we currently offer regional provider KMS with dedicated key segregation. BYOK is available for enterprise deals but requires a separate ops integration.

For the runbook, we have a short technical description and an ops checklist which Marco will pull together. We can upload everything to the Drive folder and route a DocuSign link for the DPA once we confirm the acceptable evidence.

I'll attach the SOC2 snapshot and a temporary link to the subprocessor CSV later today.

—Sarah
Head of Legal & Compliance
Northleaf Health

Attachment: soc2_snapshot_q1_2028.pdf (PDF, 1.8 MB)

Adding a couple of operational clarifications from our side that may affect what Northleaf sends: 

- For EU-covered customers we require either (A) region-qualified data egress (EU-only routing + onshore KMS) OR (B) an agreed SFTP export lane with a contractual SLA for data export/escrow. The subprocessor list should call out any party with access to raw prompts/outputs.
- The audit log extract needs to show both the toggle and the owner (service account vs. human) for model-improvement jobs. If the extract only shows job IDs, we will need a mapping table.
- For BYOK we can proceed but timelines typically add 6-8 weeks for key exchange and validation; if that's a blocker, provider KMS with key segregation is workable for the first contract term.

I've attached a short ops-runbook-stub.txt that shows the fields we need in the audit CSV and the minimum SFTP directory layout for exports. If Northleaf can provide the CSV with those headers, security will be able to complete a reconciliation exercise quickly.

Thanks —
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi all —

Thanks for the quick turn. Per security sign-off criteria, Redwood can proceed to execute the DPA if Northleaf provides:

1) Subprocessor CSV (current roster) with the headers in ops-runbook-stub.txt (we can accept redacted contact info)
2) SOC2 Q1 2028 PDF (received — thanks)
3) Audit log extract (7-day redacted) that includes job-owner mapping or an attached mapping table
4) A commitment note (email is fine) that for the duration of the contract Northleaf will not feed Redwood tenant data into any model-improvement pipelines (this can be a short clause we append to the DPA)

Operational workaround offered: if Northleaf cannot provide BYOK within contract signing timelines, we will accept provider KMS with regional key segregation for EU accounts and the SFTP export lane described by Marissa as a compensating control; we will set a 90-day BYOK implementation milestone in the SOW.

Next steps:
- Northleaf to upload the subprocessor CSV + audit extract to the shared Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-northleaf-evidence
- Legal to circulate updated DPA and DocuSign link.

If they agree to the substitute controls above and the artifacts arrive by end-of-week, we can route for signature next week.

David Kim

Redwood Inference
